tests.name: Source, plist and packaged-default tests
tests.evidence: 11 Python tests passed; defaults are LowLatency=true, AllowUnauthenticatedLAN=true, Scale=0.40, FrameRateSpec=30:60:120, LANWebViewerEnabled=true, WebViewerTrustedLAN=true, RemoteControlEnabled=true and HttpPort=5801.

tests.name: Existing Single View authentication/reconnect/LAN/USB behavior
tests.evidence: Node wrapper test passed password challenge, security failure, reconnect budget and LAN/USB endpoint selection.

tests.name: Multi View online/offline isolation
tests.evidence: Chrome connected one real LAN RFB endpoint while a second closed endpoint remained offline; the online canvas stayed active and no page error occurred.

tests.name: Lazy/capped Multi View manager
tests.evidence: Eight cards requested against the available iPhone; exactly six sessions became live and two waited at the configured limit. This is not an eight-device physical test.

tests.name: Credential storage
tests.evidence: Browser storage contained device configuration only; no password field or value was persisted. Passwords remain in per-session tab memory.

tests.name: GitHub Actions roothide build
tests.evidence: Run 39111854823 completed successfully, including TLS lifecycle, upstream baseline, source/security tests, Theos build and package validation.

tests.name: Independent DEB validation
tests.evidence: Package com.dk.viewphone 1.2.0, iphoneos-arm64e, 206 payload entries and four signed arm64 Mach-O files validated; stopped status-bar dylib is absent.

tests.name: Upgrade and runtime on physical device
tests.evidence: Upgraded 1.1.4 to 1.2.0, resprung, observed one watchdog and one server on 5801/5901, no new SpringBoard/server report, and confirmed the old status-bar tweak file was removed.

tests.name: Web assets served by installed DEB
tests.evidence: Windows Chrome loaded the 1.2.0 Multi-Device Viewer from http://192.168.1.158:5801, opened Multi View, connected the current iPhone and rendered one canvas with zero page errors.

tests.name: Two, four, eight or twelve distinct physical iPhones
tests.evidence: Only one physical iPhone was available. Multi-device correctness across separate phones, per-device CPU/RAM, LAN bandwidth and independent touch routing remains unverified.

tests.name: Long-run memory, FPS and end-to-end latency
tests.evidence: No multi-hour leak test or glass-to-glass FPS/latency measurement was performed. The UI deliberately does not invent FPS or latency values.

tests.name: Fresh physical install defaults
tests.evidence: Source and packaged Root.plist defaults were validated. The physical device was upgraded so its saved 1.1.4 preferences were intentionally preserved rather than overwritten.
